params.body:
Sign in to gentells.com with Google, LinkedIn or Microsoft. The Observatory signs people in through the site's own OAuth server, so whoever signs in here this way also gets into the Observatory, with the access their plan or team role gives.

**Who is who** (`app/Auth/SocialIdentity.php`, `SocialAuthController`):
- An identity already linked signs in to its account.
- Otherwise the provider must vouch for the address in a field made for it: `email_verified` for Google and LinkedIn (OpenID Connect). For Microsoft the Graph address (`userPrincipalName`) is set by a tenant admin and checked by nobody, the known takeover route, so it is never trusted alone: only the signed ID token counts, a personal Microsoft account, or a work account with `xms_edov: true` and an `email` claim. A vouched address that matches an account links to it; with no account a new reader account is made on Explore, as `register` does (the Clay lead included).
- An unverified address neither links nor creates anything. A blocked account gets the same answer as a wrong password. A team account may sign in through a vouched provider.
- The intended URL survives the round trip, so a reader sent to `/login` by the Observatory's `/oauth/authorize` lands back on it.

**Account page: Sign-in methods.** Linked and available providers, Add and Remove. Linking while signed in needs a mark the redirect step set in the session, and refuses an identity that belongs to another account. Remove is refused unless another way in remains (`User::keepsAWayInWithout()`). Add is a link, not a form: the CSP's `form-action 'self'` would block a form whose redirect chain ends at the provider.

**Buttons** "Continue with Google / LinkedIn / Microsoft" above the login and register forms. A provider without credentials has no button and its routes are 404. The routes stay behind the pre-launch cover.

**Data:** `social_accounts` (unique per provider identity, one per provider per account) and `users.password_usable` (false for team accounts and accounts made through a provider; a password reset sets it true).

Packages: `laravel/socialite` ^5.31, `socialiteproviders/microsoft` ^4.10.

Tests: `tests/Feature/SocialLoginTest.php` (23): new account, link only when verified, unverified refused, known identity, blocked, linking from the account page, unlink refused without another way in, unconfigured providers absent, the intended URL. Full suite 484 of 485 (`BuildStampTest` fails on main in a worktree too). Pint clean.

On deploy: the migration runs; set `GOOGLE_CLIENT_ID`/`GOOGLE_CLIENT_SECRET`, `LINKEDIN_CLIENT_ID`/`LINKEDIN_CLIENT_SECRET`, `MICROSOFT_CLIENT_ID`/`MICROSOFT_CLIENT_SECRET` for each provider registered with redirect `https://gentells.com/auth/{google,linkedin,microsoft}/callback`. For Microsoft work accounts, add the optional ID-token claims `email` and `xms_edov`.
params.title: Sign in with Google, LinkedIn and Microsoft
